title: SpiceJet to Add 20 Aircraft and Target 200 Daily Flights Ahead of Winter Travel Rush
excerpt: The budget carrier has finalised lease agreements for 15 Boeing and five Airbus planes, with deliveries starting mid-October ahead of the Durga Puja travel surge.
body:
• SpiceJet has finalised lease agreements with three operators for 20 aircraft — 15 Boeing and five Airbus planes — under wet and damp lease arrangements
  • The fleet additions will arrive in phases between mid-October and mid-November, ahead of the Durga Puja travel peak
  • The airline plans to ramp operations to approximately 200 daily flights during the winter schedule, up from its current 11-aircraft fleet
  • Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu said the government is pushing SpiceJet to step up operations and address financial difficulties

SpiceJet has finalised lease agreements to induct 20 aircraft into its fleet ahead of India's winter travel season, as the cash-strapped budget carrier moves to nearly triple its operational capacity. The airline currently operates just 11 aircraft, down significantly from its peak fleet size.

The 20 planes — comprising 15 Boeing and five Airbus aircraft — will arrive through damp and wet lease arrangements with three operators between mid-October and mid-November, timed to the start of the Durga Puja travel period, according to The Hindu BusinessLine and Livemint.

How the Expansion Works

Under a damp lease, the lessor supplies the aircraft along with flight crew and maintenance support while SpiceJet provides cabin crew. A wet lease goes further, with the lessor operating the aircraft with its own complete crew, insurance, and maintenance cover. Both arrangements allow SpiceJet to add capacity quickly without the capital outlay of purchasing or dry-leasing planes.

Among the five Airbus aircraft, an A321 variant will be inducted, offering higher seating capacity than SpiceJet's existing narrow-body fleet of Boeing 737 MAX 8s and Q-400 turboprops. The larger aircraft will be deployed on routes with strong passenger demand.

With the expanded fleet, SpiceJet targets approximately 200 daily flights during the winter schedule — a dramatic increase that, if achieved, would restore the airline to a meaningful share of India's domestic aviation market. The carrier said the additional capacity will support operations through the winter season and into the following summer peak.

Government Pressure

"The airline has assured the government that it will improve its operations soon."

— Ram Mohan Naidu, Civil Aviation Minister

Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu, speaking on the sidelines of an industry event on Thursday, confirmed that the government is pushing SpiceJet to step up operations and address its financial issues. The airline's severe fleet reduction — from over 60 aircraft at its peak to just 11 — has drawn regulatory attention and raised questions about its long-term viability.

A Familiar Playbook

SpiceJet followed a similar expansion strategy a year ago, adding 20 aircraft to its fleet through a mix of damp-leased Boeing 737s, an Airbus A340 wide-body, and reactivated grounded jets during the same pre-winter period. Chief Business Officer Debojo Maharshi said the carrier is focusing on deploying capacity where passenger demand is strongest while expanding its network in a measured manner.

The fleet expansion comes as India's aviation market continues to grow. Airlines across the sector are adding capacity ahead of the winter travel period, when demand typically surges around major festivals and year-end holidays.

What to Watch

Whether SpiceJet can execute the fleet ramp-up on schedule and sustain 200 daily flights will depend on its ability to manage the financial burden of wet and damp lease costs alongside ongoing debt obligations. The airline's track record of seasonal expansions followed by capacity pullbacks means travellers and industry watchers will be monitoring actual deployment closely through November.
